component.name: DNF Package Manager
component.summary: Fedora updates you can see and control

description.p: The Discover alternative for Fedora KDE. Every action runs the real DNF and Flatpak commands with live output, updates install right away instead of waiting for a restart, and you choose what gets updated: everything, everything except the kernel and graphics drivers, or security fixes only.
Keep Discover for browsing apps if you like. One click turns off its update checks so you don't get duplicate notifications, and one click brings them back.

ul.li: Combined DNF, Flatpak and security-advisory updates with download previews
Update without Major: upgrade everything except the kernel, graphics drivers, firmware and bootloader
Security-only upgrades and a reboot-required banner
Guided Fedora release upgrades when a new version is out
Discover takeover, background update reminders and optional passwordless updates
Search the Fedora repositories and install RPMs, with versions and source repository shown
Flatpak manager with Flathub search, repository and COPR manager, and transaction history with undo
System information dashboard, quick tools, and light and dark themes

description.p: Adds Update without Major (upgrade everything except kernel, graphics drivers, firmware and bootloader), guided Fedora release upgrades, per-package Hold Back, repository search and install, a single update button with a favorite mode, security tags and version changes on every update, and a Clean Up preview. Security fixes: the passwordless rule now covers only exact upgrade commands, and app self-updates are verified against a SHA-256 checksum. Fixes security advisory counts on dnf5, crashes when closing during background work, and many smaller issues.
Fix terminal worker execution hang and cancel operation behavior, sync login autostart with reminder switch, and add independent Flatpak reminders.
Combined updates, upgrade previews, reboot banner, package details dialog, Settings page (Discover takeover, reminders, passwordless updates), light/dark themes, adaptive vector icons, and UI polish.
